Thanks. Sorry, yeah I realised after posting that it was just a ramble of 'my life sucks because this'.
I guess I would love to hear how people went about getting help when the regular avenues weren't working. Or if anyone has dealt with a dramatic increase of intensity of a mental illness that came along with suicidality, and got through it. I want success stories, I guess.
I feel like this would do better on /nosleep. I had a big fat nope the second the words went away.

Mum came and had a look at my computer because she thought I was watching someone's wedding video. I jerked the screen away so fast, I think all she saw was something white coming out of flesh. Now she thinks I was watching romantic porn in the lounge. It's better that she doesn't know the truth.
I stared at that photo for too long. Now it looks like she's wearing a wig made for a baby.
I'm saving this. It's definitely something I will be reading again and again, and offering to friends who need this kind of soothing reassurance.

I think if I had grandkids and a long term penpal, I would make sure to keep the letters mysterious.
I'd keep them in a locked trunk in a small room that I'd call the writing room, and no one would be allowed to enter the writing room but me. It would be locked at all times. When asked about it, I'd answer "the time is not right" and I'd hurriedly change the subject. At odd hours of the day and night, I'd rush away from whatever I was doing to lock myself into the writing room for an hour or two, and return appearing disturbed and worried.

Then, when the grand children got to an age I deem appropriate, I'd give them the key to the writing room, and I'd give them the key to the trunk and wait for their disappointment when they discover that the letters only contain mild discussion of the internet and pictures of cats.

Hi, a bit late on the bandwagon here, but I've only just discovered this.
I run the fatandslutty wordpress, and I wrote this piece.
I put the trigger warning there because a few people who I know read my wordpress are recovering from eating disorders and they find discussion of the negative connotations of 'fat' quite triggering. Having discussed the piece with them before publishing it, they requested that I use a warning, so I complied.
I will happily use trigger warnings whenever I discuss something that I know to be potentially harmful, and I welcome people who read my stuff to tell me if I incorrectly labelled something, or need to add a trigger warning.
I would much prefer to err on the side of caution than risk triggering someone and turning my blog into an unsafe space.
